Human themoregulation via the act of sweating is one of the most often overlooked anatomical advantages humans have over most other animals when it comes to long-distance running (there are not exactly many animals that can keep up with a well-trained human when it comes to running marathons). Extensive body hair would hamper with the thermoregulation, so it's not surprising that humans lost their body hair (well, most of it and most of them, at any rate).

Another thing to bear in mind that the use of body hair on primates presumably lies in a) allowing infants to cling to their mothers while the latter are using their hands for locomotion and b) camouflage in the thick jungle.
